notes.title: CAP Theorem & Consensus Proof
notes.text:
## Linearizability vs Serializability
Theorem: Under network partitions, choose between Consistency and Availability.

  • Safety: Never return an uncommitted state
  • Liveness: Every request eventually receives a response (Δt < ∞)

notes.title: Atomic File Operations & Crash Recovery Architecture
notes.text:
Atomic Persistence Protocol:
1. Serialize state to a process-scoped .tmp file and validate JSON structure.
2. Invoke fsync on the file descriptor before closing.
3. Execute atomic rename over the primary state file and update the .sha256 integrity digest.
Key Exam Takeaway: In-place file truncation is never crash-safe; atomic rename is indivisible at the filesystem inode level.
notes.contentHTML:
Atomic Persistence Protocol

To guarantee Zero Data Loss across unexpected crashes or power interruptions, the storage layer enforces a strict 3-step pipeline:

  • Step 1 (Isolated Staging): Serialize state to a process-scoped .tmp file and validate JSON structure.
  • Step 2 (Hardware Flush): Invoke fsync on the file descriptor before closing.
  • Step 3 (Atomic Swap): Execute atomic rename over the primary state file and update the .sha256 integrity digest.
Key Exam Takeaway: In-place file truncation is never crash-safe; atomic rename is indivisible at the filesystem inode level.

notes.title: Midterm Exam Formula & Theorem Checklist
notes.text:
CAP Theorem & PACELC:
In the presence of a network Partition (P), a distributed store must choose between Consistency (C) and Availability (A).
- CP Systems: ZooKeeper, etcd, Spanner (strict linearizability)
- AP Systems: Dynamo, Cassandra (eventual consistency with vector clocks)

notes.title: Transformer Scaled Dot-Product Attention
notes.text:
Scaled Dot-Product Attention:
Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q * K^T) / sqrt(d_k)) * V
- Scaling by 1 / sqrt(d_k) prevents dot products from saturating the softmax function.
- Multi-Head Attention allows attending to information from different representation subspaces simultaneously.
notes.contentHTML:
Scaled Dot-Product Attention

The core self-attention equation projects queries Q, keys K, and values V:

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax((Q · KT) / √dk) · V
  • Scaling by 1 / √d_k prevents dot products from saturating the softmax function.
  • Multi-Head Attention allows attending to information from different representation subspaces simultaneously.

flashcards.q: Why must an atomic file save call fsync() before rename()?
flashcards.a: Without fsync(), the OS page cache may reorder the directory entry rename before the file data blocks are committed to non-volatile storage, leaving a 0-byte file after power loss.
